summary:
S.J. Res. 185, introduced April 27, 2026, by Senator Kaine and cosponsors, is a joint resolution invoking Congress's war powers to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from unauthorized hostilities within or against the Islamic Republic of Iran. The Committee on Foreign Relations was discharged on May 19, 2026, and the resolution was placed on the Senate calendar (Calendar No. 415).

Section 1 sets forth findings, including that Congress holds the sole constitutional power to declare war under Article I, Section 8, Clause 11; that Congress has neither declared war on Iran nor enacted a specific statutory authorization for the use of military force within or against Iran; and that the use of military force against Iran—including enforcement of a naval blockade—constitutes the introduction of Armed Forces into hostilities within the meaning of section 4(a) of the War Powers Resolution (50 U.S.C. 1543(a)). The findings also recite that section 1013 of the Department of State Authorization Act, Fiscal Years 1984 and 1985 (50 U.S.C. 1546a) subjects such a removal measure to the expedited procedures of section 601(b) of the International Security Assistance and Arms Export Control Act of 1976 (Pub. L. 94-329).

Section 2(a) is the operative directive. Pursuant to 50 U.S.C. 1546a and in accordance with the expedited procedures of section 601(b) of Pub. L. 94-329, Congress directs the President to remove United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Iran unless such hostilities are explicitly authorized by a declaration of war or a specific authorization for use of military force. The resolution amends no provision of the U.S. Code; it operates as a privileged war-powers directive under existing statutory authority and contains no appropriation or authorization of appropriations.

Section 2(b) provides a rule of construction preserving certain activities. Nothing in the resolution may be construed to prevent the United States from: (1) defending against an attack on the United States or its personnel or facilities in other nations; (2) collecting, analyzing, or sharing intelligence with partner countries attacked by Iran since February 28, 2026, and with other nations and international organizations, regarding threats from Iran or its proxies; and (3) assisting such partner countries and other nations by intercepting retaliatory attacks by Iran or its proxies or by providing defensive materiel support for such defensive measures.

The resolution specifies no separate effective date or removal deadline, and includes no sunset provision.
